schema_review.rationale: The reusable Server migration framework registers actual PowerContext 1.3.0 through s1300 -> s1400 -> s1401 -> s1402 and actual 1.4.0 through the separate immutable r1400 -> s1400 -> s1401 -> s1402 source bridge. Original 1.3 resources and checksums remain byte-identical. Real 1.4.0 SQLite, embedded seekDB and OceanBase structures were captured from the official wheel in all twelve vector/Code configurations; provenance and exact source layouts are packaged with the bridge. The 1.4 bridge preserves current Candidate, Artifact and task data, adds the missing Topic budget/block structure, revokes old lease fences and joins the existing archive/portable-storage path. Empty retained tables align the final schema without inventing 1.3 Candidate history. Source histories retain their identity through subsequent upgrades and recovery; shared head names never authorize adopting unknown layouts. Vector profiles remain bound to historical model, profile ID, dimension, unit normalization and L2 distance, with no provider calls during maintenance. Complete schema, domain, projection, profile and retained-history checks precede startup and partial maintenance. Local SQLite and embedded seekDB startup reject an observable active maintenance lock through a read-only probe. SQLite runtime admission validates the default adjacent journal, rejecting unfinished full or partial maintenance, changed recorded revision checksums and missing required retained tables. Absent journals do not invent retention obligations; custom evidence directories require explicit operator verification and remote coordinator locks remain subject to deployment orchestration. Native read-only readiness uses a consistent snapshot and does not acquire Atomic Memory head locks; normal business transaction isolation is unchanged. Offline projection repairs retain the original locked state comparison and write-side CAS protection. Target locks, backup choices, original recovery evidence and explicit remote acknowledgments remain enforced. The installed-artifact catalog retains twelve 1.3.0 source/backend/vector/Code combinations. Embedded seekDB full-server-code and full-server-vector-code are temporarily manual-only due to native DDL waits with the available engine. Main and publication require the other ten; no manual result is needed for publication. The two deferred configurations remain unverified and are excluded from generated supported upgrade declarations. Reports retain their identities and explicitly record incomplete full-matrix acceptance. The registered 1.4.0 bridge remains implemented but is outside the CI upgrade acceptance matrix; passing this gate does not certify that path. The gate preserves source-specific Processing counters and isolates OceanBase source databases. Any failed, skipped or missing automatic case rejects publication. The policy remains upgrade-required until the exact target artifact passes the required automatic matrix and the reviewed support declaration is updated. Captured source structure, local tests and checkpoint replay are distinct from installed-release acceptance, native interruption/observer recovery and backup restoration. The Candidate generation prototype observes actual SQLite/seekDB/OceanBase migration checkpoints outside the production bundle; it does not replace frozen registrations or weaken recovery checks. Existing target schema and data formats, including batched persistence interfaces, remain governed by the shared registered path. The synchronized master adds blank-text validation at Source creation and managed worker logging. It changes neither registered table layout nor migration data encodings; existing stored Source values are not rewritten. The source bridges and frozen history remain unchanged. Compatibility commands identify Server-owned storage before opening a writable legacy profile and delegate source admission to the shared framework, including actual 1.4.0 and rejection of unknown layouts. Partial Processing and Atomic Memory projection maintenance verify the original recorded revision checksums; native admission also validates typed journal identity and its completed position against the database revision. Persisted vector profiles reject unsupported partial maintenance before plans, backups or operation evidence, including when the supplied configuration omits embeddings. These are admission-only changes; frozen migration resources, registered layouts, historical checksums and data transformations remain unchanged. PowerContext 1.4.1 assigns release-based presentation names v1_4_1_001 through v1_4_1_003 to the existing shared upgrade steps; the 1.3.0 and 1.4.0 source baselines remain independently registered. Existing revision IDs, bundle and revision checksums, accepted plan identities and journal schemas are unchanged. New Server revisions use software-version-plus-sequence names directly; software releases without storage changes may reuse the same database revision. Naming does not grant acceptance or replace source registration. Full Server status, plan, apply and verify reject unfinished Processing configuration and Atomic Memory projection journals through the same typed admission check used by partial maintenance and SQLite startup. The owning domain runner can still resume its own journal. This only changes admission; frozen revisions, journal formats, database layouts and data transformations remain unchanged. PreparedContext Receipt records the actual FTS mode on Experience search outcomes. This adds only an in-memory observation field; it does not change stored Experience rows, SQL selection, schema registrations, migration resources, or data encodings.
